title: Quadratic Bezier Splatting with Structural Initialization for Efficient Painting Rendering
claim: Baselines that rely on low-level smoothing or on a single mechanism fragment or stall; combining semantic structure with optimization gives coherent, converging results.
layout: 2 panels, left-right, image grids with row labels and ✓/✗ marks
description: The figure has two tinted panels. The left panel, green and titled 'Semantic Coarse-to-Fine', is a grid of painting renderings. The columns are Coarse, Mid, Fine, Zoom-in and Input. The rows are Image Blur, Blur-guided Strokes and Semantic Strokes, showing a pagoda scene. Red arrows labeled 'Guide' run from the blurred images to the blur-guided strokes. Blue and yellow boxes mark regions that are enlarged in the zoom-in column. Blur-guided strokes look fragmented, while semantic strokes look coherent. The right panel, blue and titled 'Model-Optimization Synergy', shows a close-up of an eye at iterations 1000 to 4000. The rows are Only Opt., Only Model and Model + Opt. Green check marks and yellow crosses with captions such as 'over-smoothing', 'well-structured', 'hard to converge' and 'well-converged' show that only the combined row succeeds at every iteration.
caption: Motivation. Left: Image-blur-based coarse-to-fine optimization mainly performs low-level smoothing and produces fragmented stroke layouts, while our semantic initialization yields more coherent multi-scale strokes. Right: Optimization alone can eventually converge but suffers from early over-smoothing, whereas model prediction alone provides good early structure but is difficult to refine. Combining semantic initialization with optimization achieves both well-structured strokes and stable convergence.
abstract: Stroke-based rendering is often optimized as a pixel-level reconstruction task. This over-reliance on global error reduction not only degrades strokes into fragmented curves due to a lack of structured planning, but also allows locally defective primitives to be concealed by overlapping layers. To address these issues, we introduce a model-guided framework for stroke-audited rendering. Our framework uses Quadratic Bezier Splatting to analytically model continuous curved strokes with efficient differentiable alpha compositing. Built on this renderer, a feedforward multi-scale stroke decoder provides a structural initialization with learned stroke-scale allocation, while test-time stroke optimization supplies the reconstruction capacity needed for high-fidelity refinement. We further propose a single-stroke audit mechanism that explicitly evaluates local stroke quality, preventing defective primitives from surviving optimization through layer-wise compensation. Compared with existing methods, our approach achieves coherent layouts, improves PSNR by up to 5.46 dB, yields a 16% more compact representation, and accelerates combined renderer forward and backward computation by a factor of 220.3.
